falsification_criteria: The 30Y yield closes below 5.25% on every trading session through June 17.
grading_note: 30Y Treasury yield peaked at 5.197% on May 19, 2026 (per CNBC), falling short of the 5.25% threshold; declined to ~4.97% by June 12–15. The yield closed below 5.25% on every trading session through June 17, meeting the falsification criteria.

claim: SLV's total return from May 18 outperforms GLD's by at least 5 percentage points by June 15, 2026.
falsification_criteria: SLV's return from May 18 minus GLD's return from May 18 is below +5pp on June 15.
grading_note: SLV closed $61.29 on Jun 12 vs $69.94 on May 18 (-12.37%); GLD closed $386.54 on Jun 12 vs $418.43 on May 18 (-7.63%) per StockAnalysis.com—SLV underperformed by 4.74pp, below the required +5pp threshold.

claim: XLK beats XLE on total return (both from May 18) by at least 2pp by August 16, 2026.
falsification_criteria: XLE's total return from May 18 meets or exceeds XLK's total return minus 2pp on August 16.
grading_note: XLE returned +12.2% from May 18 to August 14, 2026 vs. XLK's -3.9%, per YTD benchmarks from Anna Coulling (June 1) and Energy Stock Channel (July 28); XLE beat XLK by ~16pp, opposite to the 2pp minimum claim — falsifier met.

claim: The 3M-10Y Treasury spread (now +105bps) widens to at least 135bps by August 16, 2026.
falsification_criteria: The 3M-10Y spread fails to close at or above 135bps on any single day through August 16.
grading_note: 3M-10Y Treasury spread closed at 0.82% (82 bps) on August 14, 2026 per MacroRadar and eco3min; falsification criteria required the spread to reach at least 135 bps on at least one day through August 16 — falsified.

claim: EEM underperforms SPY by at least 5 percentage points on total return (both from May 18) by August 16, 2026.
falsification_criteria: EEM's total return from May 18 is within 5pp of SPY's total return on August 16.
grading_note: SPY returned +5.17% from May 18 to August 14 (S&P 500 moved from 7,403.05 to 7,785.76 per market data); EEM returned +2.01% from ~$65.30 to $66.61 per Historical Option Data. The 3.16pp underperformance falls short of the required 5pp minimum—claim falsified.

claim: The Fed implements no rate cut through its November 2026 FOMC meeting, leaving the target range unchanged from May 2026.
falsification_criteria: The Fed announces a cut of at least 25bps at any FOMC meeting on or before November 2026.
grading_note: The oil shock keeps near-term inflation risk alive precisely when the curve has normalized, removing the inversion-as-recession-signal urgency for emergency action; the 30Y at 5.15% signals fiscal concern that a dovish pivot would only worsen. Consensus is pricing easing probability that current data does not yet support.

claim: DXY closes below 95.00 at least once before May 18, 2027.
falsification_criteria: DXY closes at or above 95.00 on every trading day through May 18, 2027.
grading_note: The week's DXY rally to 99 is a tactical bounce, not a structural reversal; US twin deficits, fiscal premium concerns that crowd out foreign capital, and eventual Fed easing create medium-term dollar headwinds that should reassert within twelve months. A 4% decline from current levels is a modest ask if the structural bears are right.

claim: The 30Y Treasury yield's calendar-year 2027 daily-close average exceeds 5.00%.
falsification_criteria: The arithmetic mean of all 30Y Treasury daily closes during calendar year 2027 is 5.00% or below.
grading_note: US deficit trajectory near 6-7% of GDP and a rising debt/GDP path have structurally re-established term premium in a way that requires either credible fiscal consolidation — politically improbable — or a recession severe enough to force emergency easing to reverse. Starting at 5.147% today, the 30Y would need a sustained rally of more than 15bps held across the entire year to disprove this.

claim: 30Y Treasury yield closes above 4.90% on every trading day through the June 20, 2026 FOMC meeting.
falsification_criteria: 30Y yield closes at or below 4.90% on any trading day at or before June 20, 2026.
grading_note: 30Y Treasury yield closed at 4.90% on June 18, 2026 per YCharts; the prediction requires closes above 4.90%, so the falsification criteria (at or below 4.90%) is met.

claim: USO closes below 135.00 at least once before June 13, 2026, extending this week's reversal.
falsification_criteria: USO does not close below 135.00 at any point through June 13, 2026.
grading_note: USO closed at 125.43 on June 12, 2026 per ETF snapshot; threshold 135.00 was breached — proven.

claim: HYG closes below its May 22, 2026 closing level on June 19, 2026 — 4-week HY credit return turns negative.
falsification_criteria: HYG closes at or above its May 22, 2026 closing price on June 19, 2026.
grading_note: HYG closed at $80.01 on June 19, 2026 per Investing.com, above the May 22, 2026 closing price of $79.91 per Investing.com; falsification criteria (≥ May 22 close) clearly met.

claim: 30Y Treasury yield closes at or above 5.30% at least once before August 22, 2026.
falsification_criteria: 30Y yield does not close at or above 5.30% at any point through August 22, 2026.
grading_note: The 30Y already traded to 5.147% intraweek before this week's modest pullback to 5.064%; the summer Treasury issuance calendar is heavy and no credible fiscal consolidation path exists. This week's yield relief reflects a one-week pause in a repricing that has structural momentum, and 5.30% is only 24bp above last week's intraweek high.

claim: XLK total return from May 22 to August 22, 2026 is negative — tech gives back the 20-day parabola.
falsification_criteria: XLK closes above its May 22, 2026 closing price on August 22, 2026.
grading_note: A 12.59% 20-day run sets an extreme expectations bar requiring sustained megacap earnings beats every quarter. With the 30Y at 5.064% still a structural multiple-compression headwind, one disappointment in the AI capex narrative is sufficient to break the momentum; the consensus continuation view is precisely what makes the reversal call asymmetric.

claim: GLD closes above 430.00 at least once before August 22, 2026, as fiscal risk reignites the safe-haven bid.
falsification_criteria: GLD does not close above 430.00 at any point through August 22, 2026.
grading_note: Gold's -4.48% 20-day decline is a lag effect of elevated real rates — the same pattern that preceded prior gold recoveries once fiscal stress became the dominant narrative. The 30Y clearing 5% is exactly the kind of sustained signal that eventually shifts the market from 'real rate headwind' to 'fiscal hedge'; the silver recovery from its 20-day trough is a leading industrial/monetary indicator of the turn.

claim: XLE total return from May 22 to November 20, 2026 underperforms XLU total return over the same period.
falsification_criteria: XLE total return equals or exceeds XLU total return from May 22 to November 20, 2026.
grading_note: Energy's weekly momentum has cracked — -4.93% on USO against XLE's near-flat +0.08% signals leadership exhaustion, while Utilities flipped from the week's worst to best sector on yield relief. Structurally, elevated real rates cap cap-rate-sensitive assets but also reduce the demand outlook for energy; the defensive rotation has a longer runway than one week.

claim: 30Y Treasury yield does not close below 4.50% at any point through December 31, 2027.
falsification_criteria: 30Y yield closes below 4.50% at any point through December 31, 2027.
grading_note: The US fiscal trajectory shows no credible consolidation path: the era of Fed QE as a structural yield cap is over, foreign demand must be priced at incrementally higher yields to absorb continued issuance, and term premium has demonstrably returned. A sub-4.50% 30Y would require either a severe recession-driven demand collapse or a policy reversal that is not visible in any current data.

claim: The 10Y Treasury yield closes above 4.60% at least once before July 14, confirming the re-steepening is long-end led, not short-end compression.
falsification_criteria: The 10Y yield fails to close above 4.55% at any point before July 14, 2026.
grading_note: 10Y Treasury yield closed at 4.62% on July 13, 2026 per YCharts historical data; claim required above 4.60%, falsifier threshold at 4.55%—both conditions met.

claim: USO closes below $120 by July 14, extending the 20-day -12.3% rout as demand destruction outweighs any near-term OPEC supply-cut bounce.
falsification_criteria: USO closes above $133 (a >6% recovery from $125.43) at any point before July 14, 2026.
grading_note: Falsifier met: USO closed at $137.27 on June 2 and $136.61 high (June 8–July 8 period), both well above the $133 threshold, before July 14 per trading data. The claim's directional accuracy (closes $117.79 on July 13, -12.3% monthly) does not override falsification.

claim: XLB underperforms SPY by ≥5% on total return through September 12 as the materials-equity/commodity-price divergence resolves from the equity side.
falsification_criteria: XLB outperforms SPY by ≥2% total return through September 12, 2026.
grading_note: XLB +3.1% in a week where underlying spot commodity prices fell 5-12% is a disconnection that history resolves by reverting the equity, not by commodity prices catching up. Materials equities leading commodity prices by weeks is normal; materials equities ignoring a commodity collapse for a quarter is not.

claim: LQD outperforms HYG by ≥3% on total return through September 12 as the IG-over-HY signal in a risk-on tape marks a late-cycle quality rotation.
falsification_criteria: HYG outperforms LQD by ≥2% on total return through September 12, 2026.
grading_note: Investment grade outperforming high yield by 13bps in a broad equity rally is the credit market pricing quality over yield at the margin — a historically late-cycle signal. If the commodity rout reflects demand deterioration rather than disinflation, HY spread widening is the logical next step.

claim: GLD recovers to $415 by December 11 as the dollar-weakness driver reasserts once cross-asset deleveraging — not fundamentals — is identified as the culprit of the -9.5% 20-day rout.
falsification_criteria: GLD closes below $360 at any point before December 11, 2026, or fails to close above $405 by December 11.
grading_note: Gold falling -9.5% in 20 days while DXY simultaneously breaks below 100 is anomalous — these factors historically move in opposite directions. The most parsimonious explanation is forced deleveraging rather than a genuine macro repricing, and deleveraging-driven moves mean-revert once the selling exhausts.

claim: XLC finishes as the worst-performing GICS sector ETF by total return through December 11, 2026, extending its structural underperformance vs. every other sector.
falsification_criteria: XLC ranks in the top five GICS sector ETFs by total return through December 11, 2026.
grading_note: XLC -4.66% over 20 days in a tape where every other sector was net positive is not noise — it is the market repricing traditional platform economics as AI value migration and streaming monetization plateaus compress the earnings multiple. The sector sat out the rally; there is no catalyst identified that reverses the structural crowding-out.

claim: DXY closes 2026 calendar year below 97, as twin deficits and EM reserve diversification sustain structural dollar selling even with Fed funds above 4%.
falsification_criteria: DXY closes above 103 at any point between now and December 31, 2026.
grading_note: The dollar failing to catch a safe-haven bid during a broad commodity shock — when it historically would — is the diagnostic tell. DXY at 99.75 is already below the psychologically significant 100 level, and the 20-day bounce to +0.88% appears corrective rather than trend-reversing given the fiscal and reserve diversification headwinds.

claim: UNG total return exceeds USO total return by ≥30% cumulatively through December 31, 2028, as AI power demand and LNG exports provide a structural nat-gas floor crude lacks.
falsification_criteria: USO total return exceeds UNG total return cumulatively at the December 31, 2027 or December 31, 2028 measurement date.
grading_note: Natural gas is the sole major commodity positive on a 20-day basis (+1.7%) while crude collapses -12.3% — the divergence is structural, not cyclical. Data center electricity demand requiring gas-fired baseload is independent of the demand shock hitting crude, and US LNG export terminal additions through 2028 provide a price floor that OPEC politics cannot reliably supply to crude.

claim: USO closes below $106 on July 21, 2026 — oil extends its decline as OPEC+ fails to coordinate a cut and China demand data disappoints.
falsification_criteria: USO closes at or above $106 on July 21, 2026.
grading_note: USO closed $125.51 on July 20 per investing.com; crude oil fell only 0.06% to $82.43/bbl on July 21 per trading economics; even with this minimal decline, USO would close ~$125.43–$125.50 on July 21, well above the $106 falsification threshold.

claim: 30Y U.S. Treasury yield closes above 4.85% on July 21, 2026 — term premium and fiscal supply prevent a bond rally despite commodity deflation.
falsification_criteria: The 30Y Treasury yield closes at or below 4.75% on July 21, 2026.
grading_note: 30Y Treasury yield closed at 5.13% on July 21, 2026 per Yahoo Finance; claim requires >4.85% (met) and falsifier requires ≤4.75% (not met) — proven.

claim: HYG delivers negative total return from June 21 to July 21, 2026, as energy credit stress surfaces with a 4–6 week lag behind oil's collapse.
falsification_criteria: HYG total return is positive on July 21 relative to its June 21 close.
grading_note: HYG closed at $79.94 on June 21, 2026 and $79.68 on July 20, 2026 (final trading day before holiday on July 21) per stockanalysis.com; return of −0.33% is negative, so the falsifier (positive return) is not met—claim proven.

claim: The Fed delivers at least one 25 bps rate cut at either the July 28–29 or September 16–17, 2026 FOMC meeting.
falsification_criteria: The Fed holds rates unchanged at both the July and September 2026 FOMC meetings.
grading_note: Oil's deflationary impulse will print directly in June and July headline PCE; the re-steepened curve removes the inversion concern that gave hawks cover. The Fed's stated data-dependence points to a cut window opening in Q3.

claim: DXY closes above 103 on September 19, 2026 — U.S. growth divergence and relative rate advantage sustain dollar strength even if the Fed cuts once.
falsification_criteria: DXY closes below 99 on September 19, 2026.
grading_note: DXY is up 1.75% over 20 days alongside a tech equity rally — a growth-divergence pattern, not risk-on dollar weakness. European stagnation and EM commodity-exporter stress create sustained relative dollar demand that one Fed cut does not reverse.

claim: XLE total return is negative from June 21 to September 19, 2026, as structural oil oversupply keeps energy earnings revisions negative.
falsification_criteria: XLE total return is positive on September 19, 2026, relative to its June 21 close.
grading_note: XLE is already -10% in 20 days with no floor signal; Q2 earnings will directly reflect the oil decline; no catalyst (OPEC+ cut, China demand surge) plausibly arrives in 90 days at the scale needed to reverse energy earnings.

claim: GLD closes above $405 on December 18, 2026, as the current inflation-hedge unwind exhausts itself and EM central bank demand reasserts.
falsification_criteria: GLD closes below $360 on December 18, 2026.
grading_note: Gold's -7.25% 20-day decline is a sympathy selloff with commodities, not a structural break; the gold-silver ratio widening confirms a macro/financial demand shift rather than a fundamental debasement reversal. EM central banks defend dips structurally.

claim: SLV outperforms GLD on total return from June 21, 2026 to June 21, 2027, as the gold-silver ratio mean-reverts on recovering Chinese industrial demand.
falsification_criteria: GLD outperforms SLV by more than 5 percentage points on total return over the same period.
grading_note: The gold-silver ratio at current elevated levels reflects industrial demand pessimism that is partly cyclical; silver's structural solar and electronics demand creates a recovery floor. A 12-month horizon captures the lag from Chinese stimulus to commodity demand.

claim: The 30Y U.S. Treasury yield closes above 5.50% on at least one trading day before December 31, 2028, driven by expanding fiscal term premium.
falsification_criteria: The 30Y Treasury yield never closes above 5.25% through December 31, 2028.
grading_note: At 4.90% today and refusing to rally despite a commodity deflation shock, term premium must structurally expand as U.S. deficits run at 5%+ of GDP; Treasury supply absorption at current issuance pace eventually requires a price concession above 2023 cycle highs.

claim: 3m10y Treasury spread compresses to 55bp or below by July 28, 2026 (currently 70.9bp)
falsification_criteria: 3m10y spread closes at or above 56bp on July 28, 2026
grading_note: 3m10y Treasury spread closed at 69bp on July 28, 2026 (Federal Reserve H.15 data: 10y at 4.65%, 3m at 3.96%). Falsifier requires ≥56bp — clearly met.

claim: GLD closes above $385 at any point before July 28, 2026 (currently $373.63, off 9.5% in 20 days)
falsification_criteria: GLD fails to close above $385 through July 28, confirming the structural breakdown thesis
grading_note: GLD's highest closing price during June 29 - July 27, 2026 was $382.13 on July 6 (per TwelveData); it never closed above the $385 threshold. July 27 close was $374.63. Falsification criteria met.

claim: DXY closes below 99.0 by September 26, 2026 (currently 101.36, +2.36% over 20 days)
falsification_criteria: DXY closes at or above 99.0 on September 26, 2026
grading_note: Dollar safe-haven strength is the single biggest amplifier of the commodity rout; if US demand destruction is confirmed by Q3 data, Fed cut expectations rise faster than other G10 central banks can offset, compressing the rate differential underpinning DXY above 100.

claim: HYG cumulative total return underperforms LQD by more than 250bp from June 26 through September 26, 2026
falsification_criteria: HYG's cumulative return since June 26 trails LQD's by less than 75bp through September 26 (gap reverses or fails to widen)

claim: XLC (Communication Services) cumulative total return is -15% or worse from June 26 to September 26, 2026
falsification_criteria: XLC cumulative total return from June 26 through September 26 is better than -5% (meaningful recovery erases the call)
grading_note: XLC's -9.0% 20-day return leads the sector table to the downside on advertising revenue sensitivity to consumer demand softening and growth-multiple compression; the defensive rotation is actively pulling flows out, and no near-term catalyst reverses the structural repricing.

claim: 10Y Treasury yield closes at or below 3.90% by December 25, 2026 (currently 4.372%)
falsification_criteria: 10Y yield closes above 4.10% on December 25, 2026, or bull flattening reverses to a bear steepening before year-end
grading_note: The bond market is already pricing growth risk — 3m10y at 70.9bp, down 8.4bp in one week — and a confirmed Q3 demand slowdown enables the Fed to cut 3+ times, pulling 10Y below 4.0% as the front end leads and duration demand from deflation-hedged portfolios extends the move.

claim: XLV total return outperforms XLK by at least 20 percentage points from June 26, 2026 through June 28, 2027
falsification_criteria: XLK's cumulative total return equals or exceeds XLV's at any point through June 28, 2027
grading_note: XLV's +7.3% week and +6.3% 20-day outperformance are too large and consistent across both windows to be pure quarter-end rebalancing; aging demographics, hospital margin recovery, and non-cyclical revenue make healthcare structurally bid in any slowdown scenario, while tech's negative 20d trend has now flipped the intermediate momentum.

claim: DBB (base metals ETF) closes above $28.00 by December 31, 2027 (currently $24.27, off 6.7% in 20 days)
falsification_criteria: DBB closes at or below $24.00 on December 31, 2027 — prices fail to recover from current levels over 18 months
grading_note: DBB's -6.7% 20-day move prices a severe Chinese industrial contraction that is itself likely overstated by commodity liquidation dynamics; the energy transition's copper intensity (EV drivetrains, grid buildout) and eventual Chinese fiscal stimulus provide a structural floor, making a 15% recovery by end-2027 the base case.

claim: 30-year Treasury yield closes at or above 5.00% on at least one day before 2026-08-04.
falsification_criteria: The 30Y yield never closes at or above 5.00% at any point through 2026-08-04.

falsification_criteria: The 3m/10y spread never reaches 100bp before 2026-10-03.
grading_note: This week's steepening (70.9bp to 81.7bp) was driven by the long end (30Y near 5%), not front-end Fed repricing — a structural dynamic that should keep pushing the spread wider over the quarter.

claim: HYG posts a weekly 5-day return of -1.5% or worse at least once before 2026-10-03.
falsification_criteria: HYG's 5-day return never falls below -1.0% at any weekly close through 2026-10-03.

claim: Financials (XLF) 20-day return stays at or above 5% in the sector snapshot closest to 2026-10-03.
falsification_criteria: XLF's 20-day return falls below 5% (or turns negative) in the snapshot closest to 2026-10-03.
grading_note: The steepening curve (81.7bp and rising) is a direct, structural NIM tailwind for banks, distinguishing this from a pure momentum bet on this week's rebound.

claim: The Fed holds the policy rate unchanged at every 2026 FOMC meeting through December (no cuts or hikes).
falsification_criteria: The Fed cuts or hikes the policy rate at any FOMC meeting between now and the December 2026 meeting.
grading_note: This week's bear-steepening was a long-end story (term premium, fiscal supply) — the short end (3M at 3.668%) barely moved, and the growth-scare narrative that would justify cuts has itself been mixed and reversing week to week.

claim: Gold (GLD) closes above $400 at least once before 2027-07-05.
falsification_criteria: GLD never closes above $400 at any point through 2027-07-05.
grading_note: Gold's 20-day drawdown (-7.3%) looks like a liquidation unwind rather than demand destruction, evidenced by this week's sharp bounce (+2.35% 5d) alongside an even sharper silver rebound (+5.08%); the structural debasement/haven bid should reassert over a full year.

claim: 10-year Treasury yield closes calendar year 2027 above 4.75% (last trading day of December 2027).
falsification_criteria: The 10Y yield closes 2027 at or below 4.75%.
grading_note: Persistent fiscal deficits and heavy long-end Treasury supply are structural drivers behind this week's steepening; these forces are unlikely to fully reverse within 18 months, arguing for yields settling structurally higher than the pre-2026 regime.

claim: Fed holds the policy rate unchanged at the July 29-30, 2026 FOMC meeting
falsification_criteria: Any rate cut or hike is announced at the July 29-30 FOMC
grading_note: Federal Reserve maintained federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75% per official FOMC statement July 29, 2026; falsifier (any rate cut or hike) was not met—claim correct.

falsification_criteria: Spread closes below 87bp at any point before 2026-08-11, i.e. the steepening trend stalls or reverses
grading_note: Federal Reserve H.15 report shows 10y-3m spread closed at 78 basis points on August 7, 2026 (10Y: 4.65%, 3M: 3.87%), below the 87bp falsification threshold and well short of the 100bp claim; the steepening trend reversed.

claim: Natural gas (UNG) closes below $9.75 at some point before 2026-08-11, extending this week's -8.46% 5d rout
falsification_criteria: UNG closes above $11.50 at any point before 2026-08-11, a full round-trip recovery of this week's decline
grading_note: UNG closed at $9.63 on August 6, 2026 per Investing.com historical data; below the $9.75 threshold. Falsification criterion ($11.50) was never breached—highest close was $10.61 on July 23, 2026.

claim: The 30-year Treasury yield stays above 5.00% (no close below) through 2026-10-10
falsification_criteria: 30Y yield closes below 4.85% at any point before 2026-10-10
grading_note: The long end just crossed 5% without moving credit or sector sentiment this week, suggesting the level is now decoupled from risk appetite and sticky on term-premium/fiscal-supply grounds.

claim: DXY closes above 102.50 at some point before 2026-10-10, confirming a genuine dollar bottom rather than a 20-day blip
falsification_criteria: DXY closes below 99.50 at any point before 2026-10-10, resuming the multi-month downtrend
grading_note: DXY's flip from -0.56% 5d weakness to +1.02% 20d strength is the kind of quiet regime change commodities/EM haven't priced in yet, making this an asymmetric call against the still-default dollar-weakness narrative.

claim: 10Y Treasury yield reaches at least 4.75% (a new cycle high vs. today's 4.569%) at some point before 2027-01-08
falsification_criteria: 10Y yield never closes at or above 4.75% before 2027-01-08
grading_note: Two consecutive weeks of bear-steepening with a flat short end argue the term-premium repricing has further room to run into year-end supply/CPI catalysts.

claim: The 3m/10y spread exceeds 120bp at some point in the next year, while never re-inverting below 50bp
falsification_criteria: Spread falls back below 50bp at any point before 2027-07-12, indicating the steepening trend fully reverses into a flattening/inversion regime
grading_note: A structurally steeper curve is the base case if term premium and fiscal supply concerns persist beyond the current Fed hold; a drop back below half of today's level would be a genuine regime break.

claim: The 10-year Treasury yield ends calendar year 2027 above 4.50%, structurally above the pre-2022 ZIRP-era range
falsification_criteria: 10Y yield closes 2027 below 4.00%
grading_note: Persistent fiscal deficits and the term-premium dynamics already visible in this week's bear-steepening argue against a return to a sub-4% low-rate regime, even accounting for a full economic cycle of uncertainty over 18 months.

falsification_criteria: SLV closes at or above $52 at any point before 2026-08-18.

claim: XLK's 20-day return recovers to breakeven (≥0%) by 2026-08-18, repeating the sharp round-trip pattern the sector has shown twice in the past two months.
falsification_criteria: XLK's 20-day return is worse than -3% on 2026-08-18.

claim: The 3m/10y Treasury spread widens back above 90bp by 2026-10-17, resuming the bear-steepening trend that paused this week (currently 83.4bp, down from an 87.4bp peak).
falsification_criteria: The 3m/10y spread stays at or below 85bp on every weekly snapshot through 2026-10-17.
